A bed with a tough plastic mattress filled with water.
The collection of words a person knows and uses.
(linguistics) Language as spoken or written by the common people.
A period during which a war is in progress in a particular place.
(slang) Broke; having no money.

Only, simply, merely.
Without others or anything further; exclusively.

Located outside a country or place, especially one's own.
Belonging to another country; foreign.
A person, animal, plant, or other thing which is from outside the family, group, organization, or territory under consideration.
A person whom one does not know; a person who is neither a friend nor an acquaintance.
A person from a foreign country.
of, concerned with, or preoccupied with a world different from the tangible world
Abusive language.

An ordered list of objects, typically indexed with natural numbers.

Any of various data structures designed to hold multiple elements of the same type; especially, a data structure that holds these elements in adjacent memory locations so that they may be retrieved using numeric indices.
A fellow member of a profession, staff, academic faculty or other organization; an associate, a workmate.

Acting to supplement.

Although; despite the fact that; even though.

Tending or used to cure disease or relieve pain.
partly frozen, crystalline state of water that falls from the atmosphere as precipitation in flakes; falling of such flakes; accumulation of them as a white layer

Money, riches, or wealth, especially when seen as having a corrupting effect or causing greed, or obtained in an underhanded manner.
In time to come; in some future time or state.
wealthy and industrialized; not third-world.

The process of bringing an object back to its original state; the process of restoring something.

The midday Islamic prayer.

Wealth.
Riches; a great amount of valuable assets or material possessions.
One's wealth; the amount of money one has, especially if it is vast.
A vast sum of money; (by extension) a large amount of something.

Any plant of the genus Plantago, with a rosette of sessile leaves about 10 cm (4") long with a narrow part instead of a petiole, and with a spike inflorescence with the flower spacing varying widely among the species. See also psyllium.
A yellow-brown, addictive narcotic drug obtained from the dried juice of unripe pods of the opium poppy, Papaver somniferum, and containing alkaloids such as morphine, codeine, and papaverine.
The quality of being possible.
A thing or circumstance that is welcome and makes life a little easier or more pleasant; a public facility.
Relief from work or activity by sleeping; sleep.

Any of the Papally-endorsed military expeditions undertaken by the Christians of Latin Europe in the 11th to 13th centuries to reconquer the Levant from the Muslims, as well as expeditions along the Baltic Sea and against the Cathars.
A group of people within hearing; specifically, a large gathering of people listening to or watching a performance, speech, etc.
Someone who views a spectacle; an onlooker or spectator.

A en given name.
Capable of producing great physical force.
Of land, etc.: capable of growing abundant crops; productive.
(literary, of things that grow) Abundant, luxuriant.
Highly fertile; able to produce offspring.
A sum of money or other property that a natural or legal person borrows from another with the condition that it be returned or repaid over time or at a later date (sometimes with interest).
An ancient Roman family name, notably that of Julius Caesar.
Having experience and skill in a subject.
The cardinal number immediately following sixty and preceding sixty-two.
adult male animal

negative effects caused by heavy drinking

The use of property, or an existing mortgage, as security for a loan, etc.
A meal of fried sausages, bacon, eggs, etc.

One whose activities make use of the scientific method to answer questions regarding the measurable universe. A scientist may be involved in original research, or make use of the results of the research of others.
A specialist in a particular branch of knowledge.
An expert in a particular field, especially as called upon to provide comment or opinion in the media; a commentator, a critic.
An educated scholar of Islamic law; a member of the ulema class
A basket, pen or enclosure for birds or small animals.

A group of similar things, either growing together, or in a cluster or clump, usually fastened together.
bunch of grapes
Any of several woody climbing vines, of the genus Wisteria, native to the East Asian countries of China, Korea, and Japan and the eastern United States.
(botany) An indeterminate inflorescence in which the flowers are arranged along a single central axis.
A supreme commander of the armed forces of a country, especially one who is also a political leader.
A student or professor of biology; one versed in the science of biology.
A type of religious painting portraying a saint or scene from Scripture, often done on wooden panels.
A cylinder of tobacco rolled and wrapped with an outer covering of tobacco leaves, intended to be smoked.
A shallow ulceration or lesion, usually involving skin or epithelial tissue.
The removal of sediment caused by swiftly moving water.

Engrossing, that sustains someone's interest.

impossible to pardon; impossible to excuse or justify

Applied to the case (as the fourth case of Latin, Lithuanian and Greek nouns) which expresses the immediate object on which the action or influence of a transitive verb has its limited influence. Other parts of speech, including secondary or predicate direct objects, will also influence a sentence’s construction. In German the case used for direct objects.
to set in a cast
The system of springs and shock absorbers connected to the wheels in an automobile, which allows the vehicle to move smoothly with reduced shock to its occupants.
A contrivance (sordine), as in a pianoforte, to deaden vibrations; or, as in other pieces of mechanism, to check some action at a particular time.
A device used to suppress ("snub") voltage transients in electrical systems, pressure transients in fluid systems, or excess force or rapid movement in mechanical systems.
